newsitem.title: UK: Labour playing gesture politics on pay - UK's Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Labour playing gesture politics on pay - UK's Clarke.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Wednesday accused the opposition Labour Party of playing "gesture politics" by saying it would freeze the pay of MPs and senior civil servants next year if it came to power.

In media interviews on Wednesday, Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown claimed the freeze, which would also apply to judges and military top brass, was necessary to set an example in the light of the high public sector borrowing requirement.
But Clarke told BBC radio the government had traditionally implemented the recommendations of the independent Top Salaries Review Board.
The cabinet would consider this year's recommendations from the board on Thursday, and would take "sensible decisions", Clarke said.
"At the first sign of pressure, Gordon starts making populist remarks," he said.
